sanskrit_verse:
आज्ञासंपादिनीं दक्षां वीरसूं प्रियवादिनीम् ।
त्यजन् दाप्यस् तृतीयांशम् अद्रव्यो भरणं स्त्रियाः ॥७६॥
transliteration: ājñāsaṃpādinīṃ dakṣāṃ vīrasūṃ priyavādinīm / tyajan dāpyas tṛtīyāṃśam adravyo bharaṇaṃ striyāḥ // YajñS_1.76
sph_interpretive_translation: He who abandons a woman who is obedient to commands, capable in action, valorous in spirit, and speaks affectionately—such a man shall compensate one-third of her sustenance cost, even if he has no wealth.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The husband holds positional authority but not absolute dominion over the wife's existential alignment.
Causation: Abandonment disrupts the sacred union and creates measurable energetic imbalance requiring rectification.
Capacity-based responsibility: Liability is proportionate to capacity; inability does not negate duty but adjusts form of restitution.
Restoration logic: Compensation ensures reintegration of the abandoned party into functional societal rhythm.
Consciousness alignment: Legal consequence aligns perpetrator’s consciousness with dharmic integrity through completion.
executable_legal_axioms: IF male partner abandons female partner AND female partner exhibits ājñāsaṃpādinī, dakṣā, vīrasū, priyavādinī traits THEN calculate sustenance value AND assign one-third as base compensation.
IF abandoning party lacks financial assets THEN obligation shifts to service-based or community-integrated repayment aligned with dharma-karma exchange protocol.
IF abandonment causes measurable disruption in social-economic flow THEN initiate restorative mediation via local dharma-adhikari until equilibrium restored.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that spousal abandonment triggers mandatory compensation regardless of economic status. The court must assess both material loss and energetic dissonance caused by severance of sacred bond. Judgment must prioritize restoration of woman's socio-economic stability rather than punitive measures against the abandoning spouse.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This ruling reflects pramāṇa-based causality where abandonment directly results in dependency and disruption. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential breakdown of household harmony leading to societal burden. Responsibility is proportional and completion-focused, not punitive. True nyāya realigns displaced energy without inflicting further suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate compulsory mediation between parties under guidance of certified dharma-adhikari.
Establish monthly contribution plan toward sustenance fund, adjusted for payer’s actual earning capacity.
Assign voluntary community service hours equivalent to unpaid debt until full restitution achieved.
Enroll abandoning party in svadhyaya program for consciousness recalibration regarding relational dharma.
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this law stands executed. Justice flows from consciousness alignment, not coercion. Wealth or its absence cannot absolve duty. Reality remains non-punitive, ever-restoring. Consciousness alone is the ultimate Adjudicator.
